Description:
Romería – meaning “pilgrimage” – is the final film in Simón‘s semi-autobiographical trilogy, which includes Summer 1993 and Alcarràs, and explores themes of belonging, family history and memory.

Discovering that she needs the signature of her paternal grandparents for a scholarship application, she travels to Spain’s Atlantic coast to meet the family she’s never known, unsure if she will be welcomed. Name: Jonathan Swift Festival: And Then There Was Gulliver
Description:
In this funny and entertaining show, we see Swift during his time as a press advisor to Robert Harley’s London government (1711-1714); his ‘banishment’ to Dublin as Dean in Saint Patrick’s Cathedral, Dublin (1713); his A Modest Proposal satire that called for the eating of Irish children; his political agitation in Dublin; and the secret publication of Gulliver’s Travels (1726) which was an instant success, but was so controversial that it was never published under Swift’s name while he was alive.

Written by Gerry Mullins for the Jonathan Swift Festival & 300 years of Gulliver’s Travels.

Name: Jonathan Swift Festival: Walking Tour with Saint Patrick’s Hospital
Description:
Led by Andrew White, Archivist at St Patrick’s Mental Health Services, this walking tour traces Swift’s deep connections to Dublin – from his years as Dean and his advocacy for the poor, to his enduring influence on Irish literature and society.

The walking tour concludes with a guided visit to Saint Patrick’s Cathedral, where an expert guide will bring to life the Cathedral’s stunning Gothic architecture, historic monuments, and Swift’s lasting imprint on this iconic landmark.

The tour begins at St Patrick’s University Hospital and ends at Saint Patrick’s Cathedral. The full experience lasts approximately one hour.

Free event, booking required.

Experience the spine-tingling thrill of exploring this architectural marvel in complete darkness, with only the echo of your footsteps and the distant chiming of bells.

Discover the life of Jonathan Swift and his connections to Saint Patrick’s Cathedral as you walk through 800 years of Irish history at this very unique experience.

Name: Jonathan Swift Festival: Gulliver’s Travels & Vivaldi’s Four Seasons
Description:
Opening the programme is the overture from Messiah, first performed in Dublin in 1742. Handel had intended it for St Patrick’s Cathedral, but permission was refused by its then Dean, a certain Jonathan Swift, and the premiere instead took place in the Music Hall on Fishamble Street.
 
Georg Philipp Telemann’s Gulliver Suite, written shortly after the publication of Swift’s novel, transforms its fantastical worlds into musical form. 
 
The evening culminates in Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons, here presented with texts by Jonathan Swift.
